            flat 'address'. Normalized on create (trimmed, whitespace collapsed,

          maxLength: 255
          pattern: '.*\S.*'

        addressLine2:

              type: string

              title: Customer code

            fiscalYear:
              title: Fiscal year
              description: >-

## Summary

I implemented the `capacityWarning` flag so it's `true` when an owner's city already holds **40–49** owners at creation time (approaching the hard limit of 50), while the existing hard rejection at 50 (HTTP 409) is unchanged.

Changes made:

1. **`OwnerRestControllerV1.java`** — Added a `CITY_CAPACITY_WARNING_THRESHOLD = 40` constant. Captured the existing per-city count (`cityOwnerCount`) into a variable reused by both the hard check and the new warning, and set `owner.setCapacityWarning(cityOwnerCount >= 40)` alongside where the other warning flags are set at create time. (At that point the count is guaranteed < 50, since ≥50 already returned 409.)

2. **`Owner.java`** — Added the persisted `capacityWarning` `Boolean` field (`@Column(name = "capacity_warning")`) with getter/setter, mirroring `bulkSignupWarning`.

3. **`openapi.yml`** — Added the read-only `capacityWarning` boolean to the owner schema, so the generated `OwnerDto` exposes it (MapStruct auto-maps the same-named field, matching how `bulkSignupWarning` works).

4. **Schema files** (`db/h2`, `db/hsqldb`, `db/mysql`, `db/postgres`) — Added the `capacity_warning` column to the `owners` table so the flag survives the create→read round trip the test exercises.

The flag is stored on the owner at creation, so the test's `GET /api/owners/{id}` reads back `capacityWarning: true` after filling a fresh city to 40 and creating the 41st owner.
